$comment: Closed WebView2 bridge protocol v1. The native host accepts requests only from the exact bundled HTTPS origin. Ping, jobs, and player requests are limited to 256 UTF-8 bytes; delivery requests use 512 UTF-8 bytes with 1 MiB responses; ping and jobs use 4096-byte responses, comparison requests use 4 KiB with 1 MiB responses, project, timeline, and thumbnail requests use 96 KiB with 1 MiB responses, transcript requests use 16 KiB with 4 MiB responses, analysis requests use 64 KiB with 4 MiB responses, review requests use 24 KiB with 1 MiB responses and 16 KiB review text, and player responses share the existing 64 MiB ingest recovery envelope. The native host authorizes its current Windows actor for every protected operation and every media GET; actor identity is never accepted from Web messages, and any requested acting role is untrusted intent revalidated against current native assignments. Analysis reads require project viewing authority, analysis decisions require analysis-decision authority, and every mutation pins the analysis revision ID plus digest; topic updates also pin the metadata revision ID. Analysis adoption targets are native-owned and never accepted from Web messages. Analysis adoption and topic edits are staged with persisted=false and adoptionPersistence=notPersisted; persistence remains a separate explicit workflow. Sensitivity findings expose only classification, reason code, source binding, and source time, never matched values. Review mutations and comparisons pin exact composition-version IDs and full digests, while rational time remains reduced integer evidence; delivery snapshots expose only natively revalidated full-digest evidence and preserve that machine QC still requires human review, has no approved numeric thresholds, and cannot independently authorize delivery. Comparisons expose only durable composition evidence and mark unsupported semantic features unavailable instead of inferring them. Source media crosses this boundary only as an opaque candidate ID, and player media uses project, kind, artifact, and digest-bound references on the reserved intercepted HTTPS media origin. Raw paths, storage references, arbitrary URLs, download capabilities, SIDs, commands, authentication secrets or values, process output, prompt or response content, template filesystem locations, and sensitive host data are prohibited.
title: WebBridgeMessage

stitchProtocolLimits.$comment: FR-035 GUI. stitch.pickClip and stitch.run use 1 KiB (1024) request and 4096 response UTF-8 ceilings, including envelopes. Responses always contain a closed result object, never an error envelope. The current native actor must have ExportComposition; denial opens no dialog. Opening/Closing cross this boundary only as opaque process-lifetime clipIds plus a bare fileName without directories; the main video only as the project, execution, artifact and digest of an output listed in a validated stored result. Output paths are chosen in the native save dialog and never sent to the Web. One stitch runs at a time. Nothing is registered, delivered or evaluated.

stitchPickClipResult.$comment: selected requires clipId and fileName (no directory, at most 255 characters); every other status has both null.

stitchRunResult.$comment: completed requires outputFileName, manifestFileName (bare file names) and durationSeconds; failed requires a stitch.* code other than stitch.usage; every other field is null.

sourceOnlyProtocolLimits.$comment: pipeline.read/regenerate/retry/cancel use exactly 1 KiB (1024) request and 8 MiB (8388608) response UTF-8 ceilings, including envelopes. Responses always contain result {status,snapshot}, never an error envelope. The current native actor must have ViewProject for reads and Editor/CreateCompositionVersion for commands; no renderer-supplied identity or approval exists. Consumers correlate requestId and method and the exact requested project. Retry returns a new execution; regeneration returns a new execution with the exact requested parent. Cancel checks the current execution/revision before signaling and awaits native cleanup. With no pipeline, commands are unavailable; saved snapshots can still be read through the real stores/result service. The entire result is projected through SourceOnlyResult.ToWebDto with camelCase properties; nested evaluation is a JSON object, never a string. Native recovery locators are excluded. previousResult is only an explicitly earlier stored same-project result that passed file/DB validation, not a result inferred from the current working copy. Result validity is not QC success or publication/delivery approval. Invalid descriptors can remain visible with resultStatus=invalid, but cannot authorize media. Generated media uses the separate reserved source-only URL below, GET only, MP4/PNG only, a held validated artifact stream and the existing single-byte-range rules. All malformed source-only URLs are intercepted, never fetched remotely.

pipelineRegenerateParams.$comment: Regeneration is not reconciliation: native rejects a current ReconciliationRequired phase or a canonical current result with stagingCleanupRequired=true or ReconciliationRequired (generationDisposition=ReconciliationRequired or nonempty reconciliationArtifacts), even if no root job is busy. Rejection is conflict with snapshot=null and accepts no new execution/job or cleanup side effects. The native pipeline must repeat these checks under its acceptance gate, alongside exact parent/settings checks.

sourceOnlyVersionEntry.$comment: One past composition version. No file path, storage reference or artifact content crosses this boundary.

sourceOnlyVersionsResult.$comment: Read-only past-version list. Reading it never mutates a version, a working copy or an artifact, and it never authorizes media. workingCopyRevision is the head revision a subsequent pipeline.restore must pin.

sourceOnlyBridgeResult.$comment: available requires a nonnull snapshot with resultStatus=none or valid. invalid permits snapshot=null, or a diagnostic snapshot with resultStatus=invalid and a safe canonical-codec result DTO or null. Consumers retain diagnostic descriptors but revoke previously verified media on invalid; descriptors are never media authorization. notFound/conflict/forbidden/unavailable require snapshot=null. The native media factory independently rejects an invalid result on every GET, including an unchanged artifact in an invalid set.

sourceOnlySnapshot.$comment: All bindings are native stored identities. Consumers verify a current result's six binding fields against this snapshot. previousResult must be a validated strictly earlier stored execution in the same project, with a different executionId and binding.versionId/versionDigest exactly equal to parentVersionId/parentDigest. No parent or no valid exact-parent result means previousResult=null; never select an unrelated older/latest-valid result or infer one from the working copy. Cross-field equality and persisted acceptance-time ordering are enforced by native consumers. PascalCase phase is the exact SourceOnlyExecutionPhase name. An invalid result may have a safe descriptor or null, never usable media.

sourceOnlyTime.$comment: Unlike legacy bridge rationalTime, result-codec rationals are JSON safe integers, not strings. Native consumers additionally enforce reduced positive-rate form.

sourceOnlyEvaluation.$comment: Exact nested AutomatedEvaluationRun canonical JSON. Its own codec replays rules, counts, target bindings, timestamps and digest; the uppercase statuses are distinct from PascalCase warning DTO statuses.

reconciliationArtifacts.$comment: Canonical diagnostic references include Delivery as well as Render/Evidence. A reconciliation reference does not prove completed delivery or grant media access, approval, or any mutation authority.

ancillaryArtifacts.$comment: Artifacts that were actually written and promoted. A kind the pipeline could not write is reported as an omission entry naming that kind, not as an empty artifact.

rationalTime.$comment: The native writer emits reduced signed-Int64 rationals. Consumers additionally enforce Int64 bounds, positive rate, and greatest-common-divisor 1 because JSON Schema cannot express that arithmetic invariant.

reviewText.$comment: Native and Web consumers additionally require trimmed nonblank valid Unicode and enforce the exact 16 KiB UTF-8 byte limit.

reviewOutputTime.$comment: The exact nonnegative reduced signed-Int64 output time. Native and Web consumers enforce Int64 bounds and greatest-common-divisor 1.

reviewCompositionChange.$comment: Consumers enforce the null/index combination for added, removed, moved, and modified kinds and reject duplicate element IDs.

reviewAction.$comment: actorRoles is the native-authorized set available to the current actor for this operation. Consumers require a nonempty canonical subset only for authorized actions and an empty array otherwise.

reviewSnapshot.$comment: Consumers enforce state-metadata nullability, current-target action precedence, approval validity against exact version ID plus full digest, direct-parent bindings, canonical action order, and action-role consistency.

comparisonReadParams.$comment: Both exact immutable composition versions are identified by canonical IDs and full lowercase SHA-256 content digests.

comparisonFeatureAvailability.$comment: These semantic categories are not durably retrievable for an arbitrary composition version and must never be inferred from generic elements or suggestion IDs.

comparisonTimeRange.$comment: Consumers enforce positive duration; output starts are nonnegative while source starts may be negative.

comparisonUsedSourceRange.$comment: The sourceSpanId and exact source/output ranges are durable provenance evidence for one composition element; no asset equivalence is inferred.

comparisonVersion.$comment: A private-safe exact-version projection. Playback duration is the maximum output-range end, or 0/1 for an empty version. Consumers reject duplicate element IDs and invalid rational ranges.

comparisonAdoptionChange.$comment: Consumers enforce the exact null combination for adopted, removed, and replaced changes and reject duplicate element IDs.

comparison.$comment: Consumers bind both snapshots to the requested IDs and full digests, validate ordered composition changes, reject duplicate element or adoption-change IDs, and require identical snapshots with empty changes when both version IDs are the same.

playerSnapshot.$comment: Consumers semantically verify digest/reference bindings, contiguous proxy intervals, monotonic source mappings, waveform channel cardinality, canonical sprite grids, and the final half-open proxy end.

digest.$comment: The exact playerSnapshot.evidenceDigest. The compact wire key keeps every nonnegative Int32 proxyFrameSequence within the 256-byte request limit.

transcriptTimeRange.$comment: The native writer emits a positive duration and a non-overflowing end; consumers enforce those arithmetic invariants.

timelineTimeRange.$comment: Consumers enforce positive duration. Output starts are nonnegative; SourceSpan starts may be negative.

transcriptSpeaker.$comment: Consumers additionally verify performer bindings and exact full-name, role, surname, and confirmation projections.

transcriptToken.$comment: Consumers verify that a timed token lies within its utterance and that effectiveSeekSourceTime is exactly the token start or parent utterance start.

transcriptUtterance.$comment: Consumers verify canonical hierarchy IDs, source-span uniqueness, monotonic timing, confidence, and consistent speaker projections.

transcriptTermCandidate.$comment: Rule-derived term candidates intentionally have no invented confidence classification; consumers verify token, source-span, and observed-text bindings.

transcriptInvalidation.$comment: Consumers verify the canonical node order and exact stale, recomputation, and manual-rebinding sets for edited versus unedited snapshots.

transcriptSnapshot.$comment: Native snapshots are authoritative. Consumers reject duplicate hierarchy IDs, broken cross-references, invalid OCC evidence, decided candidates still listed as pending, and inconsistent diff/stale/invalidation evidence.

timelineElement.$comment: Consumers enforce unique stable IDs, a contiguous output sequence from zero, positive durations, and a non-null equal-duration sourceRange only for SourceSpan origins.

timelineSplitOperation.$comment: Consumers enforce a positive canonical splitOffset and a distinct rightElementId.

timelineApplyParams.$comment: The native host replays the complete non-empty operation batch on a detached WorkingCopy and performs one atomic optimistic-concurrency checkpoint of the immutable version and updated working copy.

analysisDecisionParams.$comment: The Web supplies only candidate identity, analysis OCC evidence, and a reason. Element IDs, cue IDs, split offsets, transcript targets, and every other adoption target are native-owned and prohibited by additionalProperties=false.

analysisTopicUpdate.$comment: Exactly one topic metadata field is changed per request.

analysisTimeRange.$comment: The native writer emits a positive duration and non-overflowing end; consumers enforce those arithmetic invariants.

analysisSpeaker.$comment: Speaker editing remains on the canonical transcript path; this projection binds the current display to a source-time range for integrated review.

analysisDecision.$comment: Consumers enforce decision/status consistency and require exactly one native adoption output shape for adopted decisions.

analysisCandidate.$comment: Consumers enforce matching producer/payload discriminators, display-kind/suggestion-kind mappings, decision consistency, current-only actions, and canAdopt=false for technical warnings.

analysisSensitivityFinding.$comment: Matched values, offsets, paths, and host data are intentionally absent. Only safe classification and source-time evidence cross the bridge.

analysisStagedChange.$comment: Every adoption or topic edit is explicitly nonpersistent; persistence is a separate workflow.

analysisSnapshot.$comment: Native snapshots are authoritative. Consumers verify unique identities, cross-reference integrity, producer/payload consistency, source revision binding, decision state, sensitivity reason mapping, and nonpersistent staging.

thumbnailSnapshot.$comment: The evidence digest binds the exact durable source, source rights, source PTS index, proxy frame map, U-007 player evidence, and every trusted approved template/profile/layout option. No recommendation or score is present.

deliveryReadParams.$comment: outputTime is optional lookup intent represented explicitly as null or one exact nonnegative reduced rational.

deliveryRights.$comment: Evidence presence is exposed without leaking its path or arbitrary reference. Per-asset publication permission is distinct from project publicationScope.

deliveryQualityControl.$comment: Successful machine evidence does not apply approved numeric thresholds and cannot independently authorize delivery; every available result still requires human review.

deliveryTrace.$comment: The resolved SourceSpan alternative preserves exact rational output/source times; notFound is an explicit half-open-range miss and never invents an origin.

deliverySnapshot.$comment: The native host validates all artifact, graph, timeline, QC, approval, source-span, rights, and version bindings before emitting this allowlisted snapshot. Storage references and download capabilities are intentionally absent.

layoutProtocolLimits.$comment: layout.read and layout.apply requests retain the 64 KiB well-formed UTF-8 limit and responses the 4 MiB limit, including optional durableSubtitles metadata. Native code enforces exact Int64 bounds, reduced rationals, normalized-rectangle arithmetic, total keyframe count <= 256, verified composition lineage, aggregate/cue optimistic concurrency, and response bounds before committing mutations. Actor identity, face/provider evidence, paths, arbitrary persistence commands, and render commands never cross this boundary.

layoutText.$comment: Native code additionally requires trimmed nonblank well-formed Unicode and enforces the exact 16 KiB UTF-8 byte limit.

layoutRational.$comment: The numerator and positive denominator are canonical signed-Int64 strings. Native and Web consumers additionally enforce Int64 bounds and greatest-common-divisor 1.

layoutPositiveRational.$comment: The positive numerator and denominator are canonical signed-Int64 strings. Native and Web consumers additionally enforce Int64 bounds and greatest-common-divisor 1.

layoutNormalizedRect.$comment: Native and Web consumers additionally enforce x,y >= 0, x+width <= 1, y+height <= 1, exact rational arithmetic, and exact pixel alignment where pixels are emitted.

layoutTimeRange.$comment: Native and Web consumers additionally enforce a strictly positive duration using exact rational arithmetic.

layoutManualOperation.$comment: The four stack/background modes require exactly two sources; all other modes require exactly one. fixedTemplatePlacement alone requires templateId.

layoutKeyframeOperation.$comment: Native and Web consumers additionally enforce at most 256 keyframes across all segments, exact segment coverage, ordering, and track continuity.

layoutReadParams.$comment: Omitting latestInBranch preserves exact reads: the optional paired expectedVersionId/expectedVersionDigest selects that exact same-project version, never its child. latestInBranch is optional true-only, read-only, and requires BOTH pins. The durable provider validates that exact requested version and digest FIRST, then resolves its verified branch and returns the observed saved head. A generated root or any known journal child may be pinned; native-only composition dictionary entries alone are not branch membership proof. Unknown project/version returns notFound, wrong exact digest conflict, invalid parameters invalid. The legacy session provider returns unavailable for latestInBranch. evaluationTime retains its existing shape but does not re-evaluate durable subtitle snapshots. Unpinned reads retain default-branch behavior.

layoutApplyParams.$comment: expectedRevision is aggregate optimistic-concurrency evidence; cue edits independently pin the current immutable cue revision ID and digest. The version pair remains optional in the legacy single-branch contract but is mandatory for every durable mutation and legacy multi-branch mutation. latestInBranch and every other unknown key are forbidden. Non-head versions cannot be mutated, except that an exact idempotent request retry returns its original committed child and row metadata without advancing the branch. Durable editSubtitle ACKs follow commit; legacy edits remain notPersisted. No read or edit starts rendering, changes settings, updates the working copy, or grants approval.

layoutResolvedGeometry.$comment: pixels is the authoritative native exact-rational projection of rect, not browser floating-point geometry.

layoutOutput.$comment: Native and Web consumers enforce width/height == aspectWidth/aspectHeight and aspectWidth:aspectHeight == 9:16 or 16:9 by exact cross multiplication. 16:9 is a genuine subtitle-only workspace with manualSelection=null and no keyframe tracks, never a fabricated vertical plan.

layoutProjection.$comment: When snapshot.subtitleOnly=true, regions is the subtitle/graphic subset of the actual layout identified by layoutSpecId. Video geometry is intentionally not projected; no video crop or manual plan is invented or rounded.

layoutSubtitleDisplay.$comment: Each option is an explicit SubtitleDisplayProfile and selected-Cue projection evaluated by the native SubtitleDisplayPolicy. The UI does not infer modes from a digest.

oneOf.$comment: This is immutable delivery evidence only. Selecting either variant does not trigger rendering or fabricate a burn-in switch.

layoutSnapshot.$comment: This aggregate is a native-authoritative projection. persistence is persisted ONLY when sibling result.durableSubtitles has sequence > 0 and its headVersionId/headVersionDigest/sequence exactly match this compositionVersionId/compositionVersionDigest/revision. Otherwise it is notPersisted, including legacy responses, sequence 0 and historical exact reads whose branch head is newer. persisted attests recorded subtitle edits, NOT manual-layout persistence, rendering, delivery or approval. Durable metadata is NEVER placed inside this snapshot. Journal snapshot-v1 hashing uses the original metadata-free Available(snapshot) serialization with notPersisted, preserving stable replay hashes.

subtitleOnly.$comment: Optional capability restriction: no manualSelection or keyframe tracks; vertical manual-layout/keyframe mutations are unavailable. Always true for 16:9; may also be true for a 9:16 subtitle-only projection whose video geometry is not representable by this editor.

layoutDurableSubtitles.$comment: Only the durable service emits this read/commit receipt. rootVersionId is the ORIGINAL generated branch root, including a short's own root, not the overall landscape ancestor. headVersionDigest is the head composition ContentDigest (not the full snapshot digest). sequence counts committed edits from that root; journalDigest is the corresponding final row RecordDigest, null exactly for sequence 0. At sequence 0 rootVersionId equals headVersionId; otherwise they differ. Reads describe the observed current branch head even when returning an exact historical snapshot. Apply and idempotent replay receipts describe that operation's committed prefix, not necessarily the latest head. Clients correlate requestId/method/project, check the expected branch root (a child request requires previously accepted native branch evidence), and for latest reads require headVersionId/headVersionDigest/sequence to equal the returned snapshot version/digest/revision. Exact reads still require the requested version/digest, and must not treat a different advertised head as that snapshot. No requestedVersionId echo is needed: the correlated request retains both pins.

settingsProtocolLimits.$comment: All project, global, and file settings requests retain the 64 KiB UTF-8 limit and responses the 4 MiB limit. Native validation rejects duplicate and unknown properties, noncanonical IDs, versions, digests and Int64 strings, and numeric overflow. Profile version components are nonnegative Int32 values. Setting types, ranges and allowlists are validated against the existing profile. Global parameters never contain projectId; only file parameters allow projectId=null. The five expected fields bind the target scope's current identity, never another scope's revision. File hashes identify the original bytes, not canonicalized text. No filesystem location, file body, exception body, SQL or arbitrary command is exposed. These additional methods describe the protocol only, not runtime availability.

settingsSnapshot.$comment: definitionCount is derived from the native profile inventory and equals definitions.length; resets restore the immutable project-initial snapshot.

settingsUpdateParams.$comment: All expected fields form the optimistic-concurrency identity.

settingsGlobalSnapshot.$comment: The same inventory and identity fields as settingsSnapshot, with projectId=null for global scope. initialValues and initialSnapshotDigest are the profile's initial defaults; definitionCount equals definitions.length. Global revision is independent of every project's revision.

settingsFileExportParams.$comment: projectId=null selects global scope. expectedFileSha256=null means create only if absent; an existing file requires overwriteRequired and confirmation with its current hash. A changed hash after confirmation yields conflict.

settingsFilePreviewParams.$comment: Preview binds to the current target scope and all five expected identity fields without updating stored state.

settingsFileApplyParams.$comment: Apply revalidates both the target mutation identity and the required SHA-256 of the original preview bytes before updating stored state.

settingsFileResult.$comment: available always includes a scope-bound snapshot and a SHA-256 of the original file bytes. Export/apply snapshots are saved state; preview alone carries candidate values. Every failure has snapshot=null. Only overwriteRequired returns the current file hash for confirmation; every other failure has fileSha256=null.

settingsFilePreviewResponse.$comment: An available preview snapshot never replaces saved state: revision and initialValues remain bound to the target's current state, and only values and snapshotDigest describe the candidate. fileSha256 identifies the original bytes to confirm on apply.
